title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma takes pains to deliver a slasher fan's dream
gist: A review of Jane Schoenbrun's meta-slasher film Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, notable for reviving the pre-CGI matte-painting technique and for a fan-informed, emotionally driven approach to the genre.

insights.claim: Jane Schoenbrun's Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma is a meta-slasher starring Hannah Einbinder and Gillian Anderson whose opening sequence was designed using insights gathered from horror convention-goers.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Culture piece; minimal investor relevance beyond noting fan-driven creative development.

insights.claim: The production designers revived the pre-CGI matte-painting technique—painting backdrops on glass with blank areas for actors—despite no living filmmaker knowing exactly how 1960s filmmakers made it work, using five paintings by scenic artist Joel Rodriguez.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Illustrates a practical-effects revival as a counterpoint to CGI—of niche cultural, not market, interest.
insights.locator: Matte paintings add to the fantasy

insights.claim: Schoenbrun has no interest in more Camp Miasma films but would consider directing a Nightmare on Elm Street reboot that Paramount is currently seeking a director for, only with maximum creative control.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Minor IP note: Paramount actively developing a Nightmare on Elm Street reboot.
